events.line: A late frost caught the seedlings. Fleece would have saved them, as everyone said afterwards.
The slugs held a banquet overnight. Beer traps, eggshells, language: nothing worked.
A glut of courgettes. You left carrier bags on doorsteps and rang no bells.
A hosepipe ban. The water butt did its best.
Autumn show day. Your beetroot took a card and the neighbours took notes.
Blight got the maincrop potatoes after a damp week. Out came the bonfire.
Pigeons discovered the brassicas and told their friends.
The forcing shed paid off: pink rhubarb stalks in the dark, picked by candlelight, and top price at the gate.

upgrades.name: A row of water butts
upgrades.text: A dry spell does less harm when you have kept the rain.

upgrades.name: More raised beds
upgrades.text: More veg, more seed, more weeding.

upgrades.name: A wormery and compost bays
upgrades.text: Nothing goes to waste, and nothing grows quite as fast.

asks.title: The allotment committee
asks.text: The committee at {deed} has a waiting list of forty and a plot you are not using to the full. It has been mentioned at the meeting, in the passive voice.

options.label: Offer a corner to the next on the list
options.say: A grateful neighbour with a bag of onion sets and a lot of opinions. The committee approves.

options.label: Put more in and prove you are using it
options.say: Rows of everything. The committee comes to see, and says nothing, which is as good as a rosette.

options.label: Say you will come to the next meeting
options.say: You do not come to the next meeting.
